scope: K0A inference hardware and runtime preflight only; no model download, adapter implementation, or K0B work

integrated_gpu.name: AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics
integrated_gpu.vram_reported_by_wmi: 512 MB; WMI value is not treated as dedicated VRAM

wsl.evidence: WSL reports only the stopped Docker Desktop utility distribution; no regular Linux distribution was available for a GPU smoke test.

docker.evidence: The knowledge image accepted --gpus all and exposed NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all, but no /dev/nvidia* nodes were visible and the image has no torch; usable CUDA was not proven.

evidence.fact: Official vLLM installation guidance supports Linux and states that vLLM does not support Windows natively; Windows requires a compatible Linux environment such as WSL.
The RTX 3060 Laptop GPU reports compute capability 8.6, above the official NVIDIA compute capability 7.5+ requirement; this is a hardware threshold only, not proof that the current host can run vLLM.
Native Windows is therefore not a supported local vLLM path, and the available WSL/Docker setup did not provide a verified CUDA device inside the knowledge image.

vllm.target_runtime: Linux host with NVIDIA CUDA and verified GPU device visibility
vllm.fallback_policy: Keep llama.cpp as a later fallback decision only after a documented vLLM suitability failure; do not silently switch runtimes during K0A.

embedding.weight_size_observed: 1.19 GB model.safetensors on an earlier Hugging Face tree revision; current revision pin was resolved during K0C review
embedding.fit_assessment: Likely fits the 6 GiB GPU by checkpoint size alone, but CUDA load and throughput are unverified because torch is absent from the current project environment.

reranker.weight_size_observed: 2.27 GB model.safetensors; 2.29 GB repository on the Hugging Face tree
reranker.fit_assessment: Likely fits the 6 GiB GPU alone, but actual load, precision choice, and concurrent-memory behavior are unverified.

generator.documented_serving: vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 with an OpenAI-compatible endpoint
generator.bf16_vram_assessment: Approximately 9 GB for the original BF16 4B model according to the Qwen model-card material; this exceeds the measured 6 GiB laptop GPU before KV-cache and runtime overhead.
generator.fit_assessment: Does not fit the measured 6 GiB GPU as the selected BF16 target. A quantized model would be a separate explicit model decision and is not selected by this preflight.

recommended_execution.embedding: Retain Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B as the target; validate on a controlled Linux/CUDA host before adding an adapter.
recommended_execution.reranker: Retain BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 as the target; validate memory and latency on the same controlled Linux/CUDA host.
recommended_execution.generator: Run Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 through vLLM only on a controlled Linux NVIDIA host with sufficient VRAM; do not load the BF16 target on this 6 GiB laptop and do not switch to a quantized alternative in K0A.

dependency_plan.plan: Add heavyweight torch/transformers/SentenceTransformers dependencies only to an isolated inference profile after the Linux smoke test; keep the baseline knowledge service importable without model weights.
Choose either FlagEmbedding or a direct Transformers adapter after an isolated benchmark; do not install both into the baseline service by default.
Run vLLM as the separately provisioned inference runtime and connect through its OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint; the knowledge service should not download generator weights during ordinary startup.
Pin model revisions, runtime versions, CUDA image, and quantization only in the next implementation step after hardware is selected; this artifact intentionally records no cache or weight path.

blockers: Official vLLM support is Linux-oriented and native Windows is unsupported.
No regular WSL2 Linux distribution is installed; only the stopped docker-desktop utility distribution is listed.
Docker GPU allocation was accepted, but no NVIDIA device nodes or torch were visible in the current knowledge image, so usable CUDA was not verified.
The laptop exposes 6 GiB VRAM, below the approximately 9 GiB BF16 fit estimate for the selected 4B generator, before runtime overhead.
The current project environment has no torch and the host has no nvcc; no model load or throughput benchmark is therefore meaningful yet.
No model weights or caches were downloaded during K0A.
